preserves_php_only.instructions: Does this PHP chunk keep all server-side logic in PHP with zero JavaScript/TypeScript porting? Flag any evidence that PHP business logic, DB access, auth, session, or email logic was converted or delegated to .js/.ts. Inline <script> in a view template is ALLOWED and does not count as porting.

criteria.true: All logic remains in PHP; no require/include of JS for server behavior; inline scripts stay inline in PHP views
criteria.false: PHP logic converted to JS/TS, server behavior delegated to client scripts, or foreign language constructs embedded as server logic

single_domain_coherence.instructions: Read CHUNK OUTLINE roles. If roles are aggregator/domain services: score whether the chunk cleanly separates a monolith into thin bootstrap + one-domain files. If roles are controller/view: score whether controller/view are properly separated (controller = logic only, view = presentation only) without re-blending concerns. Fail only for wrong boundaries, mixed roles, or an unsplit multi-responsibility structure.

criteria.true: For service split: aggregator thin + each service one domain. For view extract: controller is logic-only and view is presentation-only with clear boundary
criteria.false: Boundaries wrong, roles mixed (e.g. controller still contains bulk HTML, view still does DB/redirects, or services still god-files)

contract_surface_intact.instructions: Do the callable/contract surfaces look intact for existing callers? For controllers: URL entry point still works, POST/GET handlers and redirects preserved. For views: template is still require-able and uses preloaded variables. For services: top-level named PHP functions with stable names/signatures. Fail if APIs were reshaped, renamed, or wrapped in ways that break callers.

criteria.true: Entry points, function names, and require contracts look preserved for legacy callers
criteria.false: Broken require paths, missing redirects/handlers, renamed/removed public functions, or class/namespace wrapping that breaks callers

bootstrap_safe.instructions: Is load-time wiring safe? For aggregator/bootstrap: minimal session/DB + require_once only. For controller: auth/session/POST handling then require view as last step, no harmful double-emit. For view template: safe requires of header/navbar/footer with correct __DIR__ paths, no side effects that conflict with controller. Flag fatal risks (wrong paths, header after output, recursive requires).

criteria.true: Wiring and requires are safe; controller then view load order is correct; no fatal path/side-effect risks
criteria.false: Broken requires, output before header(), conflicting session/bootstrap, or view performing controller responsibilities at load

refactor_chunk_verdict.instructions: Overall verdict for this chunk as a single refactoring unit under strict PHP-preservation guardrails. Judge ONLY structural chunk success for its action type (split_monolith, extract_view_template, etc.): PHP-only preserved, contracts intact, boundaries correct for the action, load/require safe. Residual debt tags (dead_code, type_safety, internal_srp, size) are follow-up work and do NOT by themselves block 'verified'. Use 'needs_work' only for meaningful structural problems still present. Use 'failed' only for guardrail violations.

criteria.verified: Action-appropriate structure achieved (split or controller/view extract), PHP-only preserved, contracts intact, requires/redirects safe — residual debt may remain as follow-up
criteria.needs_work: Directionally correct but meaningful structural issues remain (controller/view still blended, fat aggregator, broken boundary) — fix before verify
criteria.failed: Guardrail violation (JS porting of server logic), broken contract/require surface, or still an unsplit monolith — do not mark verified

residual_debt_notes.instructions: Primary residual debt remaining after this chunk (pick the dominant one).

criteria.none: No significant residual debt for this file at chunk scope
criteria.dead_code: Still has unused/debug/commented-out code — schedule remove_dead_code pass
criteria.type_safety: Still lacks PHP 8.2 types/strict equality — schedule add_type_declarations pass
criteria.internal_srp: Boundaries OK but functions/sections inside still blur sub-concerns — optional internal cleanup later
criteria.size: Still very large for one concern — consider a follow-up split only if needed
